175	def _validate_split_proportions(
176	    plan_name: Any,
177	    ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction],
178	    total: int,
179	    set_totals: dict[str, int],
180	    category_totals: Counter[str],
181	    set_distributions: dict[str, Counter[str]],
182	) -> None:
183	    """Reject a plan whose saved members break the saved ratio contract.
184	
185	    The statistics already agree with the members at this point, but that
186	    alone does not prove the proportions held: members moved between sets
187	    together with adjusted counts would otherwise read and export as a
188	    sound plan.  The same rule construction guarantees is enforced here,
189	    using only the members, labels and ratios saved in the plan:
190	
191	    * for the plan as a whole (``total`` members) and, separately,
192	    * for every category (its members summed across the three sets),
193	
194	    each set's actual count must satisfy
195	    ``|actual - range_total * ratio| < 1`` exactly.  An integral
196	    expectation therefore has to be met exactly, while a non-integral one
197	    accepts either floor or ceil (the rounding direction is free); a
198	    discrepancy of exactly one is always rejected.  Ratios are exact
199	    rationals, so a decimal and the equal fraction give the same answer.
200	    """
201	
202	    def fail(set_name: str, scope: str, actual: int, expected: Fraction) -> None:
203	        raise SplitError(
204	            f"Split plan {plan_name!r} is corrupted: {set_name} violates the "
205	            f"saved ratio for {scope}: actual count {actual}, expected "
206	            f"{_format_expectation(expected)}"
207	        )
208	
209	    # Whole-plan counts first.
210	    for j, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES):
211	        actual = set_totals[set_name]
212	        expected = Fraction(total) * ratios[j]
213	        if abs(Fraction(actual) - expected) >= 1:
214	            fail(set_name, "the overall count", actual, expected)
215	
216	    # Then each category on its own: a balanced total can still hide a
217	    # class whose samples were shifted between sets.
218	    for category in sorted(category_totals, key=_category_sort_key):
219	        category_total = category_totals[category]
220	        scope = "the unlabeled category" if category == "" else f"category {category!r}"
221	        for j, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES):
222	            actual = set_distributions[set_name].get(category, 0)
223	            expected = Fraction(category_total) * ratios[j]
224	            if abs(Fraction(actual) - expected) >= 1:
225	                fail(set_name, scope, actual, expected)
226	
227	
228	def _category_sort_key(category: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
229	    return (0, "") if category == "" else (1, category)

232	class DatasetStore:
233	    def __init__(self, root: Path) -> None:
234	        self.root = root.resolve()
235	        self.state_directory = self.root / STATE_DIRECTORY
236	        self.manifest_path = self.state_directory / MANIFEST_NAME
237	        self.splits_directory = self.state_directory / SPLITS_DIRECTORY
238	        self.batches_path = self.state_directory / BATCHES_NAME
239	        self.lock_path = self.state_directory / LOCK_NAME
240	        self.transaction_path = self.state_directory / TRANSACTION_NAME
241	        # A crash mid-commit can leave a prepared transaction; finish it
242	        # before any operation observes the workspace.
243	        self._recover_if_needed()
244	
245	    def initialize(self) -> None:
246	        # The empty-manifest decision is made under the workspace lock so a
247	        # concurrent first import cannot have its sample replaced by an empty
248	        # dataset created from a stale "manifest missing" observation.
249	        with self._locked(create=True):
250	            if not self.manifest_path.exists():
251	                self._write_json_atomic(
252	                    self.manifest_path, {"schema_version": 1, "items": []}
253	                )
254	            else:
255	                # An existing manifest is never rebuilt, emptied or
256	                # normalized away — but initializing over a structurally
257	                # broken one must not report success, so the corruption is
258	                # surfaced here exactly as for any other operation.
259	                self._read()
260	
261	    def add(self, source: Path, label: str | None = None) -> ImportResult:
262	        # The label is validated before anything else — before the source
263	        # is even looked at — so an illegal label fails this call outright
264	        # and can never reach the manifest, not even on a re-import of
265	        # already registered content (which would otherwise report a
266	        # harmless "already present" success).
267	        _validate_import_label(label)
268	        self.initialize()
269	        file_path = source.resolve(strict=True)
270	        if not file_path.is_file():
271	            raise ValueError(f"Not a regular file: {source}")
272	        # Hashing is pure I/O on the source file; do it before taking the
273	        # workspace lock so concurrent imports of different files hash in
274	        # parallel and only serialize for the manifest check-and-commit.
275	        # The digest and the size must describe one stable file: the read
276	        # fails if the file's identity, size or modification time changes
277	        # around or during the read, so a source being rewritten or
278	        # replaced is rejected instead of registering a digest/size pair
279	        # that never coexisted.
280	        digest, size = self._read_stable(file_path, str(file_path))
281	        with self._locked(create=True):
282	            manifest = self._read()
283	            if any(item["sha256"] == digest for item in manifest["items"]):
284	                # Re-import never overwrites the registered source, label or
285	                # revision: the first report of a digest owns its metadata.
286	                return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=False)
287	            manifest["items"].append(
288	                {
289	                    "sha256": digest,
290	                    "source": str(file_path),
291	                    "size": size,
292	                    "label": label,
293	                }
294	            )
295	            manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
296	            # Commit through the same journal as batches so the import is
297	            # crash-safe and cannot clobber a batch committed concurrently.
298	            self._commit(manifest, self._read_history())
299	            return ImportResult(digest=digest, added=True)

301	    def import_directory(
302	        self, source: Path, label: str | None = None, recursive: bool = False
303	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
304	        """Import every accepted image file under a source directory at once.
305	
306	        Candidates are regular files (never symlinks or other entry types)
307	        whose lower-cased extension is one of :data:`IMAGE_EXTENSIONS`;
308	        recursion stays on the top level unless ``recursive`` is set and
309	        never descends through symlinked directories.  They are ordered by
310	        path relative to the source directory, with ``/`` separators,
311	        compared by Unicode code point.
312	
313	        Every candidate is read in full and identified by its full
314	        SHA-256 digest.  A digest already in the workspace, or first seen
315	        on an earlier candidate in this same import, is reported as a
316	        duplicate: the earliest sorted candidate owns the registration and
317	        later paths never overwrite its source or label.  The supplied
318	        label is attached only to genuinely new samples; ``None`` and the
319	        empty string both mean unlabeled.
320	
321	        The whole batch commits as one journal transaction.  The import
322	        fails entirely (no new samples) when the label is not a string or
323	        ``None``, when the source is missing or not a directory, a
324	        directory that should be visited cannot be scanned,
325	        a candidate cannot be read in full, a candidate's identity,
326	        size or modification time changes while it is being read, or a
327	        subdirectory confirmed as a real directory is replaced by a
328	        symbolic link before its scan or before its candidates finish
329	        reading — the link target's images are never imported or even
330	        reported as duplicates.  The label check comes first of all, so
331	        an illegal label fails the call even when the directory is empty
332	        or every candidate is already registered.
333	        """
334	        _validate_import_label(label)
335	        self.initialize()
336	        source_path = Path(source)
337	        if not source_path.exists():
338	            raise ValueError(f"source directory does not exist: {source}")
339	        if not source_path.is_dir():
340	            raise ValueError(f"source is not a directory: {source}")
341	        root = source_path.resolve()
342	
343	        rel_paths, confirmed_dirs = self._scan_image_files(root, recursive)
344	        # Read (and re-stat) every candidate before taking the workspace
345	        # lock: I/O overlaps with peers, and a file that changes mid-read
346	        # fails the whole batch before anything is committed.  A confirmed
347	        # subdirectory swapped for a symlink is never read through: every
348	        # candidate's ancestor directories are re-checked before it is
349	        # opened, the open itself is pinned to the confirmed ancestor
350	        # directories with O_NOFOLLOW descriptors, and the confirmed
351	        # directories are checked once more after all reads, so the link
352	        # target's images cannot be imported or even reported as
353	        # duplicates.
354	        candidates = []
355	        for rel_path in rel_paths:
356	            ancestor = root
357	            for part in Path(rel_path).parts[:-1]:
358	                ancestor = ancestor / part
359	                self._raise_if_now_symlink(ancestor)
360	            candidates.append(self._read_candidate(root / rel_path, rel_path))
361	        for directory in confirmed_dirs:
362	            self._raise_if_now_symlink(directory)
363	
364	        with self._locked(create=True):
365	            manifest = self._read()
366	            history = self._read_history()
367	            known = {item["sha256"] for item in manifest["items"]}
368	
369	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
370	            new_items: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
371	            for rel_path, abs_path, digest, size in candidates:
372	                if digest in known:
373	                    status = "duplicate"
374	                else:
375	                    status = "added"
376	                    known.add(digest)
377	                    new_items.append(
378	                        {
379	                            "sha256": digest,
380	                            "source": str(abs_path.resolve()),
381	                            "size": size,
382	                            "label": label,
383	                        }
384	                    )
385	                results.append(
386	                    {"path": rel_path, "sha256": digest, "status": status}
387	                )
388	
389	            if new_items:
390	                manifest["items"].extend(new_items)
391	                manifest["items"].sort(key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
392	                # One journal commit for the whole batch: an interruption
393	                # leaves either the old state or every new sample together.
394	                self._commit(manifest, history)
395	
396	        added = sum(1 for result in results if result["status"] == "added")
397	        duplicates = len(results) - added
398	        return {
399	            "directory": str(root),
400	            "recursive": recursive,
401	            "label": label,
402	            "candidate_count": len(results),
403	            "added": added,
404	            "duplicates": duplicates,
405	            "candidates": results,
406	        }
407	
408	    def _scan_image_files(
409	        self, root: Path, recursive: bool
410	    ) -> tuple[list[str], list[Path]]:
411	        """Return accepted files and the real directories descended into.
412	
413	        The first element lists accepted files as ``/``-separated paths
414	        relative to root; the second lists every subdirectory confirmed as
415	        a real directory and descended into (empty unless ``recursive``).
416	
417	        Only real regular files qualify; symlinks and other entry types are
418	        skipped, and recursion never follows symlinked directories.  Any
419	        directory that should be visited but cannot be scanned fails the
420	        whole import with the path and reason.  Every confirmed
421	        subdirectory is opened through its pinned parent directory with
422	        ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` and scanned through that descriptor,
423	        so a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic link at any moment before
424	        or during its scan fails the whole import instead of the link
425	        target being scanned.  The confirmed list lets the caller
426	        re-verify the directories once more after the candidate reads.
427	        """
428	        rel_paths: list[str] = []
429	        confirmed_dirs: list[Path] = []
430	
431	        def classify(
432	            directory: Path, fd_or_path: Any
433	        ) -> list[tuple[str, bool, bool]]:
434	            try:
435	                entries = list(os.scandir(fd_or_path))
436	            except OSError as error:
437	                raise ValueError(
438	                    f"cannot scan directory {directory}: {error}"
439	                ) from error
440	            found: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]] = []
441	            for entry in entries:
442	                try:
443	                    is_file = entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
444	                    is_dir = (
445	                        not is_file
446	                        and recursive
447	                        and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
448	                    )
449	                except OSError as error:
450	                    raise ValueError(
451	                        f"cannot inspect entry {directory / entry.name}: {error}"
452	                    ) from error
453	                found.append((entry.name, is_file, is_dir))
454	            return found
455	
456	        def walk(
457	            directory: Path,
458	            rel_prefix: str,
459	            parent_fd: int,
460	            entries: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]],
461	        ) -> None:
462	            for name, is_file, is_dir in entries:
463	                if is_file:
464	                    if Path(name).suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS:
465	                        rel_paths.append(rel_prefix + name)
466	                elif is_dir:
467	                    subdirectory = directory / name
468	                    # Open the confirmed subdirectory through the pinned
469	                    # parent with O_NOFOLLOW and scan the descriptor
470	                    # itself: a symlink swapped onto the path by now fails
471	                    # the whole import here, and the link target is never
472	                    # scanned.
473	                    try:
474	                        child_fd = self._open_real_directory(
475	                            name, parent_fd, subdirectory
476	                        )
477	                    except OSError as error:
478	                        raise ValueError(
479	                            f"cannot scan directory {subdirectory}: {error}"
480	                        ) from error
481	                    try:
482	                        child_entries = classify(subdirectory, child_fd)
483	                        confirmed_dirs.append(subdirectory)
484	                        walk(
485	                            subdirectory,
486	                            rel_prefix + name + "/",
487	                            child_fd,
488	                            child_entries,
489	                        )
490	                    finally:
491	                        os.close(child_fd)
492	
493	        try:
494	            root_fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
495	        except OSError as error:
496	            raise ValueError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
497	        try:
498	            walk(root, "", root_fd, classify(root, root))
499	        finally:
500	            os.close(root_fd)
501	        # Unicode code point order on the slash-separated relative path.
502	        rel_paths.sort()
503	        return rel_paths, confirmed_dirs
504	
505	    @staticmethod
506	    def _open_real_directory(name: str, dir_fd: int | None, path: Path) -> int:
507	        """Open a confirmed directory, refusing a symlink swapped onto it.
508	
509	        The open uses ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` — relative to the
510	        pinned parent descriptor when ``dir_fd`` is given — so a symbolic
511	        link (or any non-directory) that replaced the confirmed directory
512	        is never descended through.  A symlink swap raises the import's
513	        "directory changed" error naming the replaced path; any other
514	        open failure propagates as the underlying :class:`OSError`.
515	        """
516	        try:
517	            return os.open(name, _DIRECTORY_OPEN_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
518	        except OSError as error:
519	            # Linux reports a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY
520	            # as ENOTDIR rather than ELOOP, so confirm via lstat() either
521	            # way.
522	            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
523	                try:
524	                    current = os.lstat(path)
525	                except OSError:
526	                    current = None
527	                if current is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
528	                    raise ValueError(
529	                        f"directory changed during import: {path} "
530	                        "is now a symbolic link"
531	                    ) from error
532	            raise
533	
534	    @staticmethod
535	    def _raise_if_now_symlink(directory: Path) -> None:
536	        """Fail if a previously confirmed real directory is now a symlink.
537	
538	        A path that vanished is left to the candidate reads (or ignored
539	        when the directory held no candidates); only the symlink swap is
540	        rejected here, because following the link would import the target's
541	        images against the no-symlinked-directories rule.
542	        """
543	        try:
544	            current = os.lstat(directory)
545	        except OSError:
546	            return
547	        if stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
548	            raise ValueError(
549	                f"directory changed during import: {directory} "
550	                "is now a symbolic link"
551	            )
552	
553	    def _read_candidate(
554	        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
555	    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
556	        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.
557	
558	        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
559	        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
560	
561	        Every ancestor directory of the candidate is re-opened from the
562	        source root with ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW``, each relative to its
563	        pinned parent, and the candidate itself is opened relative to its
564	        pinned parent directory: a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic
565	        link since the scan fails the whole import here, and the link
566	        target's images are never opened — no matter when the swap lands.
567	        """
568	        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
569	        root = path
570	        for _ in parts:
571	            root = root.parent
572	        try:
573	            fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
574	        except OSError as error:
575	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}") from error
576	        try:
577	            ancestor = root
578	            for part in parts[:-1]:
579	                ancestor = ancestor / part
580	                try:
581	                    next_fd = self._open_real_directory(part, fd, ancestor)
582	                except OSError as error:
583	                    raise ValueError(
584	                        f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}"
585	                    ) from error
586	                os.close(fd)
587	                fd = next_fd
588	            digest, size = self._read_stable(
589	                path, rel_path, dir_fd=fd, name=parts[-1]
590	            )
591	        finally:
592	            os.close(fd)
593	        return rel_path, path, digest, size
594	
595	    @staticmethod
596	    def _read_stable(
597	        path: Path,
598	        display: str,
599	        *,
600	        dir_fd: int | None = None,
601	        name: str | None = None,
602	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
603	        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.
604	
605	        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
606	        regular file: the path is lstat()ed without following symlinks
607	        and opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, the opened descriptor is
608	        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed, and the
609	        path is lstat()ed again after the read, requiring the same
610	        object with the same size and modification time.  Any identity,
611	        size or modification-time change — in-place rewrites, appends,
612	        truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing the path with
613	        another file, even one with identical content, size and mtime —
614	        fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing path, a
615	        non-regular file and any open or read error.
616	
617	        The confirm/open/prove rule itself lives in :mod:`confirmed`
618	        and is shared with the source-directory export; only the
619	        post-read stability requirement and the import wording are
620	        specific to this entry point.
621	
622	        When ``dir_fd`` and ``name`` are given (whole-directory import),
623	        the pre-open inspection and the post-read re-inspection stay on
624	        the path, but the open itself is ``name`` relative to the pinned
625	        parent directory descriptor: an ancestor directory replaced by a
626	        symbolic link can never redirect the open into the link target.
627	        """
628	        try:
629	            if dir_fd is None:
630	                opened_file = confirmed.confirm_and_open_regular(path)
631	            else:
632	                confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(path)
633	                descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
634	                opened_file = confirmed.ConfirmedOpen(
635	                    descriptor,
636	                    confirmed_status,
637	                    confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status),
638	                )
639	        except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
640	            raise _import_confirmation_error(failure, display) from failure
641	        try:
642	            digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(opened_file.descriptor)
643	        except OSError as error:
644	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
645	        # Import, unlike export, also requires the path itself to still
646	        # name the same unchanged file after the read: an in-place
647	        # rewrite, append, truncation or replacement that landed while
648	        # the bytes were streamed must not register a digest/size pair
649	        # that never coexisted.
650	        try:
651	            after = os.lstat(path)
652	        except OSError as error:
653	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
654	        if not confirmed.same_identity_size_mtime(opened_file.confirmed, after):
655	            raise ValueError(
656	                f"file changed during import: {display} "
657	                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
658	            )
659	        return digest, opened_file.confirmed.st_size
660	
661	    def summary(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
662	        self.initialize()
663	        with self._locked():
664	            items = self._read()["items"]
665	        labels = Counter(item["label"] or "unlabeled" for item in items)
666	        return {
667	            "items": len(items),
668	            "bytes": sum(item["size"] for item in items),
669	            "labels": dict(sorted(labels.items())),
670	        }
671	
672	    def find_by_label(self, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
673	        """List samples currently registered under one exact category label.
674	
675	        Matching is exact on the current manifest label: case, surrounding
676	        whitespace and path separators are all kept literally, so ``"cat"``
677	        never matches ``"Cat"`` or ``"cat "``.  The empty string queries
678	        unlabeled samples — records whose stored label is ``None`` or ``""``
679	        — and every matching record's label is reported uniformly as
680	        ``None``.  A genuine class literally named ``"unlabeled"`` is
681	        queried with that text and never mixed with unlabeled samples,
682	        unlike :meth:`summary` which merges them under one display key.
683	
684	        Each record provides the full SHA-256 digest, the source path saved
685	        at first registration, the byte size and the current label;
686	        records are sorted ascending by full digest and ``count`` always
687	        equals the list length.  The query reads the registered records
688	        only — it never opens a source file, and saved split plans' old
689	        labels are neither matched nor rewritten — so a moved, deleted or
690	        unreadable source is still found, and a batch update or undo
691	        committed before the call is immediately reflected.
692	        """
693	        if not isinstance(label, str):
694	            raise BatchError("query label must be a string")
695	        want_unlabeled = label == ""
696	        samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
697	        self.initialize()
698	        with self._locked():
699	            items = self._read()["items"]
700	        for item in items:
701	            stored = item.get("label")
702	            if want_unlabeled:
703	                if not (stored is None or stored == ""):
704	                    continue
705	                current = None
706	            else:
707	                if stored != label:
708	                    continue
709	                current = stored
710	            samples.append(
711	                {
712	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
713	                    "source": item["source"],
714	                    "size": item["size"],
715	                    "label": current,
716	                }
717	            )
718	        samples.sort(key=lambda sample: sample["sha256"])
719	        return {"label": label, "count": len(samples), "samples": samples}

734	                    return {"sha256": digest, "label": normalize_label(item.get("label"))}

745	    def submit_batch(self, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
746	        """Validate and apply a batch label update.
747	
748	        Parsing happens before the lock; inside the lock the submission
749	        runs through clearly separated stages, each with one job:
750	
751	        1. **Unknown samples** — every named digest must be registered; the
752	           first unknown one rejects the batch with nothing written.
753	        2. **Number identity** — a batch number already in history is
754	           refused outright when that history batch is damaged: it may
755	           list each sample at most once (a repeated full SHA-256 digest,
756	           however the copies differ, is corruption), and every one of
757	           its records must explicitly save both the before (``old``)
758	           and after (``new``) label (an explicit ``null``/``""`` counts
759	           as saved).  The refusals come before either verdict below.
760	           An intact known number then replays the first submission's
761	           result (same content) or conflicts (different content);
762	           neither touches the manifest.
763	        3. **Verification/classification** — each current label is read
764	           once: an expected-old mismatch rejects the batch, and the same
765	           reading decides whether that record actually changes.
766	        4. **Application** — only records classified as changed are
767	           mutated; if none are, the batch occupies no number and writes
768	           no history.
769	        5. **History and save** — the entry and result are assembled from
770	           the applied records, and manifest plus history commit together
771	           through the journal.
772	
773	        No stage mutates anything before every earlier stage has passed, so
774	        a rejection can neither leave partially updated samples nor a
775	        partial history entry.
776	        """
777	        number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
778	        with self._locked(create=True):
779	            manifest = self._read()
780	            history = self._read_history()
781	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
782	
783	            # Stage 1: every record must name a registered sample.
784	            reject_unknown_samples(records, items.__contains__)
785	
786	            # Stage 2: a known number is replayed or conflicts; a fresh
787	            # number proceeds without examining the current labels.
788	            # resolve_re_submission first refuses a damaged same-number
789	            # entry (a repeated sample digest or a record missing its
790	            # saved old/new label) before it can compare or replay
791	            # anything.
792	            existing = next(
793	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
794	                None,
795	            )
796	            replay = resolve_re_submission(number, records, existing)
797	            if replay is not None:
798	                return replay
799	
800	            # Stage 3: verify expected old labels and classify changed vs
801	            # unchanged in a single current-label pass.
802	            resolutions = verify_records(
803	                records,
804	                lambda digest: normalize_label(items[digest].get("label")),
805	            )
806	
807	            # Stage 4: apply is the only mutation.  No changes at all
808	            # occupies no batch number and writes no history.
809	            if not any(resolution.changed for resolution in resolutions):
810	                return no_changes_result(number, len(records))
811	            applied_records = apply_resolutions(resolutions, items)
812	
813	            # Stage 5: assemble history, then save manifest and history
814	            # together through the journal.
815	            entry = build_history_entry(number, applied_records)
816	            history["batches"].append(entry)
817	            self._commit(manifest, history)
818	            return result_payload(number, "applied", applied_records)
819	
820	    def undo_batch(self, number: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
821	        """Undo a successful batch by number.
822	
823	        Only samples the batch actually changed are checked: each must have
824	        the same label revision it had right after the batch (no later
825	        modification, even one that restored the same label).  Repeated
826	        undos are idempotent and do not add history.
827	
828	        Integrity comes before either verdict.  First the requested number
829	        must identify exactly one entry in the saved batch list: a second
830	        entry carrying that same number — identical content or different,
831	        adjacent or separated by other batches, already undone or not — is
832	        batch history corruption, never a first-match/last-match/active
833	        choice and never a merge.  The target batch must then list every
834	        sample exactly once, carry a sound pinned revision on each
835	        record, explicitly save both before/after labels on each record,
836	        and have every record's ``changed`` flag agree with the
837	        before/after labels saved on that same record.  A duplicated
838	        number, a duplicated digest, a bad row, a missing label field or a
839	        flag that contradicts its labels rejects the undo even when the
840	        batch is already marked undone, so corruption is never hidden
841	        behind an ``already-undone`` success or confused with a sample
842	        modified after the batch.
843	        """
844	        with self._locked(create=True):
845	            manifest = self._read()
846	            history = self._read_history()
847	            entry = find_unique_history_entry(number, history["batches"])
848	            if entry is None:
849	                raise BatchError(f"unknown batch number: {number!r}")
850	
851	            # find_unique_history_entry scans the whole list, so a second
852	            # same-number entry — adjacent or behind other batches,
853	            # identical content or different, already undone or active —
854	            # raises before this point; repeats of other numbers do not
855	            # match and stay irrelevant.
856	            #
857	            # Validate the unique target batch's integrity — one row per
858	            # sample, sound pinned revisions, both before/after labels
859	            # saved, and a changed flag that matches those labels — before
860	            # the already-undone short-circuit and the later-modification
861	            # checks: a duplicated, inconsistent or corrupt history record
862	            # is refusal, not an undo, a no-op or an unknown batch, and
863	            # nothing is rewritten.
864	            require_intact_history_records(entry)
865	            require_intact_history_revisions(entry)
866	            require_intact_history_labels(entry)
867	            require_intact_history_changes(entry)
868	
869	            if entry["undone"]:
870	                return {"batch": number, "status": "already-undone", "restored": 0}
871	
872	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
873	            for record in entry["records"]:
874	                if not record["changed"]:
875	                    continue
876	                item = items.get(record["sha256"])
877	                if item is None:
878	                    raise BatchError(
879	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
880	                        "is no longer in the manifest"
881	                    )
882	                current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
883	                # record["rev"] is now known to be a genuine non-negative
884	                # integer, so a boolean/decimal/string can never compare
885	                # equal to the sample's current revision.  The stored
886	                # after-label is normalized before comparing: history may
887	                # explicitly save either unlabeled spelling (null or ""),
888	                # and both match a sample currently unlabeled either way.
889	                if item_revision(item) != record["rev"] or current != normalize_label(
890	                    record["new"]
891	                ):
892	                    raise BatchError(
893	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
894	                        "was modified after the batch"
895	                    )
896	
897	            restored = 0
898	            for record in entry["records"]:
899	                if not record["changed"]:
900	                    continue
901	                item = items[record["sha256"]]
902	                item["label"] = record["old"]
903	                item["rev"] = item_revision(item) + 1
904	                restored += 1
905	
906	            entry["undone"] = True
907	            entry["undone_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
908	            self._commit(manifest, history)
909	            return {"batch": number, "status": "undone", "restored": restored}
910	
911	    def history(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
912	        """Return successful batch entries in submission order."""
913	        with self._locked():
914	            return self._read_history()["batches"]

917	    # Workspace locking and transactional commits

919	
920	    @contextmanager
921	    def _workspace_lock(self):
922	        """Exclusive workspace lock for check-and-write transactions.
923	
924	        ``flock`` is advisory but sufficient for local processes: holders
925	        serialize, so every read-modify-write observes the state left by the
926	        previous completed operation.
927	        """
928	        self.state_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
929	        descriptor = os.open(self.lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
930	        try:
931	            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
932	            yield
933	        finally:
934	            try:
935	                fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
936	            finally:
937	                os.close(descriptor)
938	
939	    @contextmanager
940	    def _locked(self, *, create: bool = False):
941	        """Hold the workspace lock and finish any leftover prepared journal.
942	
943	        Recovery runs once the lock is held, so a long-lived process that
944	        only imports, queries or creates plans still installs the prepared
945	        transaction of a process that crashed on this machine, without
946	        needing to reopen the workspace.
947	
948	        Read callers leave ``create`` false: on a workspace whose state
949	        directory does not yet exist there is no journal to finish and
950	        nothing for a writer to hold, so the query proceeds (and fails or
951	        reports empty exactly as before) without materializing one.
952	        """
953	        if not create and not self.state_directory.exists():
954	            yield
955	            return
956	        with self._workspace_lock():
957	            self._recover_transaction_locked()
958	            yield
959	
960	    def _recover_if_needed(self) -> None:
961	        """Finish a prepared transaction left by a crashed process."""
962	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
963	            return
964	        with self._locked():
965	            pass
966	
967	    def _recover_transaction_locked(self) -> None:
968	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
969	            return
970	        try:
971	            journal = json.loads(self.transaction_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
972	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
973	            raise BatchError(f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}") from error
974	        manifest = journal.get("manifest")
975	        history = journal.get("batches")
976	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
977	            raise BatchError("cannot recover interrupted transaction: journal is malformed")
978	        # Only install a coherent, fully valid pair, so recovery can never
979	        # replace the committed manifest with a structurally broken sample
980	        # list (a missing field, a bad field type or a duplicated digest):
981	        # the check runs before either file is rewritten, leaving both the
982	        # last committed registration and its history untouched.
983	        try:
984	            validate_manifest(manifest)
985	        except ManifestError as error:
986	            raise BatchError(
987	                f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}"
988	            ) from error
989	        validate_history(history)
990	        # Idempotent installs: both files end up at the journal's version.
991	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
992	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
993	        try:
994	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
995	        except OSError:
996	            pass
997	
998	    def _commit(self, manifest: dict[str, Any], history: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
999	        """Atomically install the new manifest and history together.
1000	
1001	        A write-ahead journal holding both full payloads is written and
1002	        fsynced first; a crash at any point leaves enough to redo the
1003	        missing install on the next open, so the two files never disagree.
1004	        """
1005	        journal = {"manifest": manifest, "batches": history}
1006	        self._write_json_atomic(self.transaction_path, journal)
1007	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
1008	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
1009	        try:
1010	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
1011	        except OSError:
1012	            pass
1013	
1014	    def _read_history(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1015	        if not self.batches_path.exists():
1016	            return empty_history()
1017	        try:
1018	            data = json.loads(self.batches_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
1019	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
1020	            raise BatchError(f"cannot read batch history: {error}") from error
1021	        return validate_history(data)

1027	    def create_split(
1028	        self, name: str, seed: int, ratios: list[float | int | str | Fraction]
1029	    ) -> SplitPlanResult:
1030	        """Create (or reuse) a named train/validation/test plan.
1031	
1032	        The plan snapshots every sample currently in the manifest.  A
1033	        second call with the same name returns the stored plan unchanged
1034	        when the inputs match; otherwise it reports a name conflict.
1035	        """
1036	        validate_name(name)
1037	        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
1038	            raise SplitError(f"Seed must be an integer, got {seed!r}")
1039	        fraction_ratios = validate_ratios(ratios)
1040	
1041	        self.initialize()
1042	        plan_path = self._split_path(name)
1043	
1044	        with self._locked(create=True):
1045	            # Sample identities and labels are read from one complete
1046	            # manifest state, so a batch committing concurrently is observed
1047	            # either entirely (all its label changes) or not at all.
1048	            items = self._read()["items"]
1049	            # assign() validates identities and performs the stratification.
1050	            assignment = assign(items, fraction_ratios, seed)
1051	
1052	            snapshot = [
1053	                {
1054	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
1055	                    "label": item.get("label"),
1056	                    "source": item.get("source"),
1057	                }
1058	                for item in sorted(items, key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
1059	            ]
1060	            plan_payload = self._build_plan(
1061	                name, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot, assignment
1062	            )
1063	
1064	            # The check-and-create is atomic under the same lock, so among
1065	            # concurrent creations of one name exactly one reports success;
1066	            # matching requests reuse it and differing ones conflict.
1067	            if plan_path.exists():
1068	                existing = self._read_split(plan_path)
1069	                if self._same_inputs(existing, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot):
1070	                    return SplitPlanResult(name=name, created=False, plan=existing)
1071	                raise SplitError(
1072	                    f"Split plan {name!r} already exists with different seed, "
1073	                    "ratios or samples; choose another name"
1074	                )
1075	
1076	            self._write_json_atomic(plan_path, plan_payload)
1077	            return SplitPlanResult(name=name, created=True, plan=plan_payload)

1091	    def _build_plan(
1092	        self,
1093	        name: str,
1094	        seed: int,
1095	        ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction],
1096	        snapshot: list[dict[str, Any]],
1097	        assignment: dict[str, str],
1098	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1099	        sets = {set_name: [] for set_name in SET_NAMES}
1100	        for sample in snapshot:
1101	            set_name = assignment[sample["sha256"]]
1102	            sets[set_name].append(
1103	                {
1104	                    "sha256": sample["sha256"],
1105	                    "label": category_name(category_key(sample["label"])),
1106	                    "source": sample["source"],
1107	                }
1108	            )
1109	
1110	        set_summaries: dict[str, Any] = {}
1111	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
1112	            members = sets[set_name]
1113	            distribution = Counter(member["label"] for member in members)
1114	            set_summaries[set_name] = {
1115	                "samples": len(members),
1116	                "distribution": dict(sorted(distribution.items())),
1117	                "members": [
1118	                    {
1119	                        "sha256": member["sha256"],
1120	                        "label": member["label"],
1121	                        "source": member["source"],
1122	                    }
1123	                    for member in members
1124	                ],
1125	            }
1126	
1127	        overall = Counter(
1128	            category_name(category_key(sample["label"])) for sample in snapshot
1129	        )
1130	        return {
1131	            "schema_version": SPLIT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
1132	            "name": name,
1133	            "seed": seed,
1134	            "ratios": {
1135	                set_name: str(ratios[i]) for i, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES)
1136	            },
1137	            "samples": {
1138	                "total": len(snapshot),
1139	                "distribution": dict(sorted(overall.items())),
1140	            },
1141	            "sets": set_summaries,
1142	        }

1144	    @staticmethod
1145	    def _same_inputs(
1146	        existing: dict[str, Any],
1147	        seed: int,
1148	        ratios: tuple[Fraction, Fraction, Fraction],
1149	        snapshot: list[dict[str, Any]],
1150	    ) -> bool:
1151	        """Whether a stored plan was created from the exact same inputs."""
1152	        if existing.get("seed") != seed:
1153	            return False
1154	        stored_ratios = existing.get("ratios")
1155	        if not isinstance(stored_ratios, dict):
1156	            return False
1157	        for i, set_name in enumerate(SET_NAMES):
1158	            stored = stored_ratios.get(set_name)
1159	            if not isinstance(stored, str) or Fraction(stored) != ratios[i]:
1160	                return False
1161	
1162	        # Reuse requires the exact same sample identities with the exact
1163	        # same creation-time labels; recorded sources are informational and
1164	        # do not participate in the identity (the snapshot itself is the
1165	        # decision input, per the feature contract).
1166	        current = sorted(
1167	            (sample["sha256"], category_name(category_key(sample.get("label"))))
1168	            for sample in snapshot
1169	        )
1170	        stored: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
1171	        sets = existing["sets"]
1172	        for set_name in SET_NAMES:
1173	            for member in sets[set_name]["members"]:
1174	                stored.append((member["sha256"], member.get("label")))
1175	        return sorted(stored) == current

1235	                )
1236	            set_distribution = _validated_distribution(
